context: Write a regex for the octet format: a whole number from 0 to 255, written without leading zeros. 0 itself is allowed, but 00, 007 and 010 are not. The regex must match the whole string, as Python's re.fullmatch does, so never write ^ or $. Use only the allowed dialect: literal characters (escape . $ ( ) [ ] { } * + ? | \ when meant literally), . for any character but a newline, \d \D \w \W \s \S, character classes like [0-9], groups (...) and (?:...), alternation |, and quantifiers * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} with counts up to 20. Anchors, lookarounds, backreferences, named groups, inline flags and lazy quantifiers are not allowed. \d means ASCII 0-9 and \w means ASCII letters, digits and underscore. The pattern may be at most 80 characters. It must accept exactly the format's strings: allowed examples include 0, 7, 42, 100, 199 and 255; rejected examples include -1, 1.5, 3a, the empty string, '1 0' and 1000. Pay attention to the boundaries: 249, 250 and 255 are allowed; 256, 260, 300, 00, 007 and 010 are not.
